children: Walmart Inc. (WMT, Financials), the largest U.S. retailer, is pushing further into restaurant delivery through a new partnership with Inspire Brands.
Dunkin' will be the first major brand to expand through the service, starting with about 150 locations inside Walmart stores before moving toward most of its roughly 10,000 locations nationwide.
The bigger story is what Walmart is trying to build around that partnership.
Customers will be able to add restaurant food and drinks to Walmart deliveries, letting the company use the same last-mile network it already operates for groceries and general merchandise.

That gives Walmart an advantage few restaurant-delivery competitors can easily copy. About 90% of the U.S. population lives within 10 miles of a Walmart store, giving the company a large existing footprint from which to expand.
If more restaurant chains join, Walmart could increase delivery frequency and make its app more useful without having to build a new logistics network from scratch.
That could eventually put more pressure on DoorDash and Uber Eats, particularly if Walmart can bundle restaurant orders with purchases customers are already making.
The next catalyst is how quickly Walmart expands beyond Dunkin' and whether other national restaurant chains join the platform.

title: Walmart Just Found a New Use for Its Delivery Network
